summary: Brian builds a five-layer 'memory stack' framework of choke points where AI's memory shortage creates pricing power, arguing the real money is in the picks-and-shovels beneath the obvious Micron trade. Top layer, interface: Rambus (RMBS, BUY), paid twice per chip via RCD chips plus royalties, with operating margin expanding from 9% to 37%, though an antitrust inquiry is open. Tools: Applied Materials (AMAT, BUY), whose HBM revenue went from ~zero to $1.5B targeting $3B; and Lam Research (LRCX, BUY), the purer memory bet, back at record revenue. Inspectors: Onto Innovation (ONTO, BUY), with a single $240M+ purchase agreement running through 2027; and KLA (KLAC, BUY), the near-monopoly in defect inspection with margins rising from 36% to 43%. Testers: Teradyne (TER, BUY), whose DRAM test revenue grew 330%+ as AI passed 60% of the business; and Advantest (ATEYY, BUY), holding ~two-thirds of chip test, though it trades over-the-counter in the US. Foundation: Besi (BESIY, BUY), the hybrid-bonding leader with orders up 104% for 2027 production, OTC in the US; Entegris (ENTG, BUY), where the most advanced 5% of wafers drive ~30% of revenue; and Kulicke & Soffa (KLIC, HOLD) — the speculative one, revenue down 57% over four years with only a 2027 HBM story, sized with discipline. His $100 model allocation: $25 tools, $25 inspectors, $22 testers, $20 foundation, $8 Rambus — 'best story, smallest bet.' He closes comparing two ETFs: DRAM (makers only) versus HBMX (makers plus suppliers). A sponsored Canadian Goldfields segment is included.
title: 99% of You Will Miss the Memory Stack (My Full Map)
